title: Precision Pays: A Fixed-Weight Boundary Loss Anchors the Precision End of a Recall–Precision Axis and Wins as the Consensus Veto under the Official BraTS-2023 Metrics
description: Preprint (Paper 2 of the BRATS auxiliary-loss program). Does adding the Kervadec boundary loss (fixed weight lambda = 0.05, acting directly on the logits, no auxiliary head) to a strong MedNeXt/nnU-Net glioma backbone improve adult glioma segmentation? Evaluated under the complete official BraTS-2023 metric set over a 5-fold held-out cross-validation on the 1196-case study set — the unified BraTS-2023 GLI download holds 1251 cases, and the 55 that never entered the nnU-Net dataset are listed one by one (trigger, git date of the triggering entry, and a fresh re-measurement of their file integrity against 55 included controls: 0 unreadable file, 0 NaN/Inf, 0 out-of-set label, 0 divergent affine) in analysis/DATASET_EXCLUSIONS.md. Against the baseline the boundary loss is not significant on any pre-specified primary or region-averaged official metric (lesion-wise Dice delta = +0.000, Holm p = 0.34; lesion-wise HD95 delta = -0.58 mm, p = 0.31), a null confirmed by a 3-seed multiseed check (paired t-test p = 0.42). Its only robust distinctive property is being the precision-oriented mirror of a signed-distance (SDT) auxiliary head — significantly more specific, fewer spurious tumor-core/enhancing lesions, lower recall — which makes it an effective connected-component consensus veto: used to veto the SDT model it removes about half of that model's false-positive lesions at negligible recall cost (lesion-wise HD95 -9.95 mm, p = 2.3e-20 over the 5-fold CV), and used as the primary model with a baseline veto it reproduces the companion paper's consensus gain (lesion-wise Dice WT +3.89 pp, p = 0.005, 3 seeds x fold 0). Reported in full as a transparent negative result, with a weight-selection robustness check ruling out mistuning. The archive bundles the manuscript (EN + FR, with both rendered PDFs), the reproducibility code, the exact result JSONs behind every reported number (including the patient-level export that carries the Figure 3-5 counts and the training-log export that carries the multiseed validation Dice), the tables, figures, the measured dataset-provenance artefacts and the verified reference list. All materials are released together under CC-BY-4.0 as a single publication record.
notes: Companion Paper 1 (DistMap / signed-distance auxiliary loss) studies the recall end of the same recall-precision axis: concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19695263, v10 published 2026-09-22 (record 22904810). The consensus figures this paper quotes from it are read from that record's section 4.6. Methodological rule: only benchmark-epoch results (300 epochs/fold, comparable to published teams) appear in the manuscript; short exploration runs are never reported. Exact statistics come from code/paper_stats.py and data/cv_paper_stats.json — regenerating tables/table_paper2.{md,tex} from that file reproduces the shipped tables byte-for-byte; multiseed figures from code/evaluate_multiseed_kervadec.py and data/multiseed_stats.json; the multiseed nnU-Net validation Dice from data/nnunet_validation_dice_multiseed.json; the patient-level counts behind the Figure 3-5 captions from data/patient_level_clean_BKD.json; the 55 exclusions from analysis/exclusions_1251_to_1196.csv. Revision v2.6 (2026-09-22): measured provenance of the 55 exclusions shipped and quoted in section 3.1 (the download holds 1251 cases, the study set 1196); cross-references to Paper 1 realigned on its published v10 (section 4.6, +4.28 pp and -17.2 mm rather than the obsolete run's +4.15 pp / -16.8 mm); two multiseed statistics restated at full precision (validation Dice mean 0.9060 rather than 0.9061, paired t-test -1.02 / p = 0.42 rather than 0.96 / p = 0.44, the published values having been computed on numbers already rounded to 4 decimals); every path quoted in the manuscript now resolves inside the archive; the shipped generators accept the command line the readme documents. No reported result changes.
